source_text:
Καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δὲ εὔσπλαγχνοι, εἰς πάντας ἐλεήμονες, ἐπιστρέφοντες τὰ ἀποπεπλανημένα, ἐπισκεπτόμενοι πάντας ἀσθενεῖς, μὴ ἀμελοῦντες χήρας ἢ ὀρφανοῦ ἢ πένητος ἀλλὰ προνοοῦντες ἀεὶ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐνώπιον θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων, ἀπεχόμενοι πάσης ὀργῆς, προσωποληψίας, κρίσεως ἀδίκου, μακρὰν ὄντες πάσης φιλαργυρίας, μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες κατά τινος, μὴ ἀπότομοι ἐν κρίσει, εἰδότες ὅτι πάντες ὀφειλέται ἐσμὲν ἁμαρτίας.
εἰ οὖν δεόμεθα τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ἡμῖν ἀφῇ, ὀφείλομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφιέναι: ἀπέναντι γὰρ τῶν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ ἐσμὲν ὀφθαλμῶν, καὶ πάντας δεῖ παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι.
οὕτως οὖν δουλεύσωμεν αὐτῷ μετὰ φόβου καὶ πάσης εὐλαβείας, καθὼς αὐτὸς ἐνετείλατο καὶ οἱ εὐαγγελισάμενοι ἡμᾶς ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, οἱ προκηρύξαντες τὴν ἔλευσιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν: ζηλωταὶ περὶ τὸ καλόν, ἀπεχόμενοι τῶν σκανδάλων καὶ τῶν ψευδαδέλφων καὶ τῶν ἐν ὑποκρίσει φερόντων τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίον, οἵτινες ἀποπλανῶσι κενοὺς ἀνθρώπους.
thought_title: Elders' duties and the duty to forgive
orientation: Polycarp is giving instructions for each group in the Philippian church, and has just addressed the younger men and virgins; now he turns to the elders.
pass_a_gloss: And the elders also must be compassionate, merciful toward all, turning back those who have wandered away, visiting all the sick, not neglecting widow or orphan or poor person but always providing for what is good before God and human beings, keeping away from all anger, partiality, unjust judgment, being far from all love of money, not quickly believing anything against anyone, not harsh in judgment, knowing that we are all debtors of sin. If therefore we ask the Lord that he forgive us, we also ought to forgive; for we are before the eyes of the Lord and God, and all must stand before the judgment seat of Christ and each one must give an account for himself. So then let us serve him with fear and all reverence, just as he commanded and the apostles who preached the gospel to us and the prophets, who proclaimed beforehand the coming of our Lord; zealous for what is good, keeping away from scandals and from false brothers and from those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy, who lead empty people astray.

choices.why: The adjective describes tender-heartedness toward others; 'compassionate' keeps the emotional warmth without importing a technical term.

choices.english: turning back those who have wandered away
choices.why: The participle plus neuter plural article denotes persons who have strayed; 'turning back' preserves the active restorative force of ἐπιστρέφω.

choices.english: always providing for what is good
choices.why: προνοέω means to take thought for or provide; 'providing for' keeps the sense of active care, and 'what is good' renders the articular neuter καλοῦ.
The glossary fixes κρίσις as 'judgment'; 'unjust' renders ἀδίκου plainly.
The genitive ἁμαρτίας is objective: we owe a debt consisting of sin; 'debtors of sin' keeps the metaphor literal.

choices.term: τῶν ἐν ὑποκρίσει φερόντων τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίον
choices.english: those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy
choices.why: φερόντων means 'bearing' or 'carrying'; the phrase describes false claimants to the Lord's name, and 'in hypocrisy' preserves the adverbial force of ἐν ὑποκρίσει.
rejected: those who hypocritically carry the Lord's name
those bearing the Lord's name falsely

bible_refs.note: πάντας δεῖ παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ
εἰ οὖν δεόμεθα τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ἡμῖν ἀφῇ, ὀφείλομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφιέναι

pass_b_english: The elders, for their part, must be compassionate and merciful toward everyone. They must turn back those who have wandered away, visit all who are sick, and not neglect the widow, the orphan, or the poor. Instead, they must always provide for what is good in the sight of God and of people. They must keep away from all anger, partiality, and unjust judgment, and stand far from every love of money. They must not be quick to believe a charge against anyone, nor harsh in judgment, because they know that we are all debtors of sin.

If, then, we ask the Lord to forgive us, we also ought to forgive. For we stand before the eyes of the Lord and God, and all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ, and each one will give an account of himself.

So then, let us serve him with fear and all reverence, just as he commanded and as the apostles who preached the gospel to us and the prophets who proclaimed beforehand the coming of our Lord commanded. Let us be zealous for what is good, keeping away from stumbling blocks, from false brothers, and from those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy and lead empty people astray.

problems.source_quote: πάντας δεῖ παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι
problems.why: The allusion is to 2 Corinthians 5:10, not Romans 14:10, 12. Romans 14:10 mentions judgment seat of God, not Christ; 2 Cor 5:10 has 'judgment seat of Christ' and giving account.
problems.ruling: τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ matches 2 Cor 5:10, not Romans 14:10 which has βήματι τοῦ θεοῦ.

problems.quote: and each one will give an account of himself (2 Corinthians 5:10)
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι
problems.why: The source echoes Romans 14:12 ('each will give account of himself to God'), not 2 Corinthians 5:10.
problems.fix: and each one will give an account of himself (Romans 14:12).
problems.ruling: Source ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι matches Romans 14:12 exactly; 2 Cor 5:10 has different wording.

problems.why: The source alludes to the judgment seat of Christ, but the English adds a specific scripture citation (2 Corinthians 5:10) that is not in the Greek source. This is an addition not present in the source text.
problems.fix: each one will give an account of himself.
problems.ruling: Greek source has no scripture citation; adding '(2 Corinthians 5:10)' misleads readers into thinking it's in the original.

problems.why: The parenthetical scripture citation is not in the Greek source and adds information not present there.
problems.fix: each one will give an account of himself.
problems.ruling: Parenthetical '(2 Corinthians 5:10)' absent from Greek source; addition misleads readers about original text content.

fixed: Removed the added scripture citation (2 Corinthians 5:10), which is not in the Greek source. The English now matches the source without the addition.

polish.changed: Broke the long elder list into clearer sentences, made the implied subject 'they' explicit, and clarified the connection between knowing we are debtors and not judging harshly.
